title: Three-Level Environment Chain with Lookup Tracing
description: Builds a three-frame environment chain (global -> mid-block -> inner-block) with shadowing and tracing. Shows how lookup walks the chain and reports hop counts for each variable access.
source: draft: opencode free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Environment class with vars dict, parent pointer, and name label. define creates binding in current scope. lookup walks parent chain with optional trace printing each hop.
assign walks chain to find existing binding and updates it in place. __repr__ shows the chain as 'name:vars -> parent...'.
Three-level program structure: global has x=1, y=2; mid-block (child of global) shadows y=20, adds z=30; inner-block (child of mid) shadows z=300, adds w=400.
Construction: glob defines x=1, y=2. mid with parent=glob defines y=20, z=30. inner with parent=mid defines z=300, w=400. Chain: inner -> mid -> global.

steps.question: At INNER, lookup('y') searches inner (not found), then mid (found y=20). How many hops, and why doesn't it reach global's y=2?
steps.answer: 2 hops: inner (1), mid (2). It stops at mid because y=20 is found there. The global y=2 is shadowed  -  lookup returns the first match, which is the innermost binding.

steps.description: Trace at INNER with trace=True: x takes 3 hops (inner->mid->global) finds 1. y takes 2 hops finds 20 in mid. z takes 1 hop finds 300 in inner. w takes 1 hop finds 400 in inner. Sum = 721.
Check w at MID: mid.lookup('w') searches mid (not found), then global (not found), parent is None, raises NameError. Inner names are invisible from outside.
Run it. glob = Environment(name='global') created.
glob.define('x', 1) sets glob.vars['x']=1.
glob.define('y', 2) sets glob.vars['y']=2.
mid = Environment(name='mid-block', parent=glob). mid.vars empty, parent=glob.
mid.define('y', 20) sets mid.vars['y']=20 (shadows global y).
mid.define('z', 30) sets mid.vars['z']=30.
inner = Environment(name='inner-block', parent=mid). inner.vars empty, parent=mid.
inner.define('z', 300) sets inner.vars['z']=300 (shadows mid z).
inner.define('w', 400) sets inner.vars['w']=400.
Print '=== Trace at INNER ==='.
inner.lookup('x', trace=True): not in inner, not in mid, found in global after 3 hops -> 1.
inner.lookup('y', trace=True): not in inner, found in mid after 2 hops -> 20.
inner.lookup('z', trace=True): found in inner after 1 hop -> 300.
inner.lookup('w', trace=True): found in inner after 1 hop -> 400.
Sum = 1+20+300+400 = 721. Prints 'INNER result: 721'.
mid.lookup('w', trace=True): not in mid, not in global, parent None. NameError caught. Prints 'As expected: undefined variable 'w''.
